name: Production Distro RC16
source: RC15 final audit; maestro-managed RC16 planning
goal: Plan and execute AIOS-body distributable user packaging and release-operation readiness without giving authority to mirror frontend, Nginx/TLS, remote signer, object storage, remote dispatch, private signing material, support upload, recovery execution, production rings, TUI projections, shell output, or model replay.
core_thesis: AIOS becomes Ubuntu-like only when a user-facing release package can be inspected, preflighted, explained, and safely denied or staged by the AIOS body using signed/hash-bound evidence and AgentCore plus SecurityExecution gates.
non_goals: Do not build mirror frontend, nginx, TLS, remote signer, object storage, or remote dispatch infrastructure in RC16 body tasks.
Do not read, copy, print, hash, move, or reference private signing material.
Do not claim GA production readiness.
Do not treat mirror reachability, signer reachability, frontend output, shell output, TUI output, model replay, object storage UI, or remote service reachability as authority.
Do not mutate production rings, upload support bundles, execute recovery, or dispatch remote fleet actions.
primary_acceptance: RC16-050 final closeout audit closes RC16 as a non-GA AIOS-body distributable packaging milestone.

The plan covers repo-local release package surface, installable media manifest, descriptor fail-closed fixtures, installer/update preflight, AgentCore/SecurityExecution binding, rollback/support package, TUI explainability, local consumer smoke, and final audit.

The plan preserves AIOS-body-only scope and keeps mirror frontend, nginx/TLS, signer infrastructure, object storage provisioning, remote dispatch, private signing material, support upload, recovery execution, and production ring mutation out of scope.
The plan keeps production_ready_claim=false until final audit proves every required gate.
